before.name: Naloxone

before.name: Midazolam
before.tldr: Midazolam is a fast, short-acting sedative. In cancer care it is used to keep people comfortable during procedures such as bronchoscopy, and in palliative care as the first medicine for sedation when suffering cannot be relieved any other way.

NICE CG112 lists oral or intranasal midazolam for children having painful procedures at minimal or moderate sedation. The Versed NDA was approved on 20 December 1985.

before.name: Posaconazole
before.tldr: Posaconazole is an antifungal medicine. Its label includes preventing mould and yeast infections in people with blood cancers whose white cells stay low for a long time after chemotherapy.
before.summary: The Noxafil label covers treatment of invasive aspergillosis, and "prophylaxis of invasive Aspergillus and Candida infections in patients who are at high risk of developing these infections due to being severely immunocompromised, such as hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) recipients with graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) or those with hematologic malignancies with prolonged neutropenia from chemotherapy", as well as oropharyngeal candidiasis. before.name: Urea cream
before.tldr: Urea cream softens thick, dry skin. Rubbed on the hands and feet from the first day of sorafenib, a 10 per cent cream made the painful hand-foot skin reaction less common in a large trial.
before.summary: A DailyMed listing for a 40% urea cream describes use for debridement of hyperkeratotic lesions and for hyperkeratotic conditions such as dry rough skin, eczema, keratoderma, corns and calluses; that listing carries no FDA application number. In a randomised open-label trial in 871 people with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma starting sorafenib (Ren et al., J Clin Oncol 2015), 10% urea-based cream three times a day from day 1 with best supportive care lowered the 12-week incidence of any-grade hand-foot skin reaction compared with best supportive care alone (56.0% vs 73.6%; odds ratio 0.457, 95% CI 0.344 to 0.608); the authors called for blinded placebo-controlled trials.
